result.markdown: --- title: "Welcome to Charting Waterloo Region!" description: "An introduction to the municipality that's a little bit country, a little bit rock 'n' roll." date: "2026-09-14" categories: [Snapshot, Demographics, Geography] image: images/thumbnail.png draft: true editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline --- ::: {.cell} ::: Waterloo Region, formally known as the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, comprises three cities and four townships. In this introductory post, we'll take a look at a few charts that highlight key differences between the Region's urban and rural constituents, differences that will be explored in more detail in future posts. Readers familiar with the Region's geography and demographics may not be surprised by the findings, but newcomers to the Region or those who haven't explored it much will see some interesting contrasts between the Region's rock 'n' roll heart and its country soul. ## An urban core with rural fringes On the map below, it appears as if the townships are chomping the smaller cities they nearly surround. Collectively, the townships cover 1,056 square km, or 77% of the Region's 1,370 square km land mass. Even the smallest township, North Dumfries, is considerably larger than Kitchener, the biggest city. Judged solely by its area then, the Region is largely rural in character. ## More cows than people?! The latest StatsCan population estimates show that Kitchener has by far the most residents in the Region, with slightly more even than the other two cities combined. Together, the cities had a population of 631,721 , making up 89% of the Region's 711,457 residents in 2025. So despite covering 77% of the Region's land, the townships contain only a sliver of its residents. Having a combined density of only 75 residents per square km, the townships contain one resident for every 26.7 city residents. With all that land and so few people, there's lots of room for cows! ## Income ## Households ## Language ::: panel-tabset ### Mother tongue is not English or French ### Is German or Pennsylvania
